name: vix_mean_reversion_intraday_v1
mechanism: On NIFTY, intraday VIX deviations anchored to the day's session-open level reflect the cumulative net put-buying pressure since 09:15. When VIX has risen > 3% from its day-open value and begins declining (2 consecutive 5-second bars), options market makers who sold puts during the fear wave start buying NIFTY futures to reduce their delta-hedge — generating a 15-30 second spot rally. The day-open anchor (vs. a rolling window) matters because institutional hedgers target their book to morning risk levels; deviations from that anchor are the directional signal, not short-term oscillations. The bearish mirror fires when VIX has been steadily crushed from open (complacency) and the first VIX uptick signals returning put demand, preceding a NIFTY correction.
core_signal_oneliner: VIX deviation from day-open anchor exceeds 3% then shows 2-bar reversal, confirming options MM delta-hedge unwind
